parts.note: reads as a small gift for a Christmas stocking, but means the figure who fills the stockings

explanation.surface: A small present to tuck into a Christmas stocking.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stocking filler' is usually a cheap little gift; here it is the person who does the filling on Christmas Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is the legendary visitor who fills children's stockings with presents.

clue.text: Employed to dry up after drink with the clergy

parts.note: tea is a common drink
'the cloth' is a traditional collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Someone helps with the washing-up after having tea with the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' stands for clergymen as a body, from their distinctive dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen cloth of this kind is used for drying dishes after a meal is eaten.

clue.text: Warning the tree is about to be taken down

definitions.text: Warning the tree is about to be taken down

parts.words: Warning the tree is about to be taken down
parts.note: describes the lumberjack's traditional shout as a tree starts to fall

explanation.surface: A shouted alert that a tree is being felled.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodcutters traditionally call out this word to warn others that a felled tree is falling.

clue.text: Suitable presents, say, for a flirtatious female

indicators.note: signals that the word for the presents is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: mink coats or stoles are fittingly luxurious gifts for such a woman

explanation.surface: Wondering what gifts would suit a flirty woman.
explanation.walkthrough: MINKS, furs given as gifts, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a cheeky, flirtatious or impudent young woman.

parts.note: conveyancers are lawyers handling property sales, but here they are vehicles that convey property, that is, goods

explanation.surface: Solicitors who handle house sales.
explanation.walkthrough: Conveyancing is the legal work of transferring property; here the conveyancers literally carry things, and an estate is property.
explanation.definitionFit: Large cars with a rear load area, built to carry luggage and belongings.

clue.text: Angelic turn of phrase initially introducing Christmas

indicators.note: a turn of the word phrase means its letters are turned about into a new order
takes the opening letters of the two words that follow it

explanation.surface: A heavenly expression used to usher in the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn of' rearranges PHRASE into SERAPH; 'initially' gives I and C from 'introducing Christmas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphs are the highest order of angels, so the adjective means angelic in nature.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to offer formally, as with a resignation or bid

explanation.surface: A delicate gift.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means easily damaged; the verb means to offer, as one may offer a payment.

clue.text: Make a hit unexpectedly by sending up crackers

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending a word up means writing it backwards

parts.note: crackers and nuts both mean mad

explanation.surface: Pulling Christmas crackers to cause a surprise sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like the Christmas novelty, but means crazy, NUTS, which 'sending up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze someone with a sudden blow or shock is to knock them senseless.

indicators.note: the word for provided is placed inside the rearranged letters
the letters of parties are put into a different order

parts.note: if means on condition that, provided

explanation.surface: Pre-dinner nibbles laid on at a range of festive parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' looks like 'supplied', but it is the conditional word; the anagram of 'parties' it sits inside makes APERITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinks taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite are appetisers in the original sense.

clue.text: Not inclined to put up, say, the tree

definitions.meaning: upright, not leaning at an angle
to raise or set up something, such as a Christmas tree

explanation.surface: Reluctant to set up the Christmas tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not inclined' suggests unwilling, but means not sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means perfectly upright; as a verb it means to build or set upright.

clue.text: Friar has Christmas tip for food container

parts.note: Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's companion
a Christmas box is a traditional gift of money to tradesmen and servants

explanation.surface: A monk receives a seasonal gratuity for a lunchbox.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas box is a seasonal tip, once given on Boxing Day. A tuck box is the case of treats a British boarding-school child keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: At British boarding schools, a box holding snacks and sweets (tuck) brought from home.

clue.text: Row after a youngster appears in panto

indicators.note: the word for row is placed following the other pieces

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a din is a noisy row

explanation.surface: A noisy disturbance follows when a boy turns up in a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line or a quarrel; it is noise, DIN. A panto is a British family Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the best-known British pantomimes, based on the tale of the boy with the magic lamp.

clue.text: Singers in church, knocking back port

indicators.note: knocking back the word for port means reading it backwards

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Church singers downing glasses of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' looks like drinking the port wine; it is the reversal, giving OIR, and 'port' is a city, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of singers, especially one performing in a church service.

parts.note: the men behind a pie made with minced meat, named after the flock-tenders

explanation.surface: The people who make the festive mince pies.
explanation.walkthrough: A mince pie is a Christmas sweet, but the pie here is the savoury one of minced lamb under mashed potato named after these men.
explanation.definitionFit: The men who tend sheep give their name to a pie of minced meat topped with potato.

definitions.meaning: a group of monks belonging to a religious order
as a verb, to arrange properly or put right

explanation.surface: A monastic celebration that is put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things properly is to put them right; whimsically it is also a group within a monastic order.

parts.note: silly means foolish
to point is to direct, and a point of the compass is a direction

explanation.surface: Daft instructions given to a cricket fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: Silly point is a cricket fielding position very close to the batsman, on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the fielder who stands in this close position is named after it.

parts.note: reads as a Christmas song, but it is Dickens's novella whose title calls it one

explanation.surface: A Christmas song with the miser Scrooge in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens's story about the miser Ebenezer Scrooge is titled as if it were a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's 1843 Christmas tale of the miser visited by ghosts is named as a seasonal song.

parts.note: suggests browsing books, but means old-fashioned schoolchildren dipping their pens

explanation.surface: Learned people of the past browsing through texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scholars' here means schoolchildren, who dipped nib pens into holes in their desks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink pots set into old school desks, into which pupils dipped their pens.

parts.note: sounds like reappointed to command, but a charge is the ammunition put in a gun

explanation.surface: Someone is reappointed to command.
explanation.walkthrough: A charge is the load of powder and shot put into a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun that has been refilled with ammunition has had its charge put in once more.

parts.note: suggests the current owners of a title, but means the things that hold Christmas presents

explanation.surface: Whoever currently holds a title or office.
explanation.definitionFit: Long socks hung up on Christmas Eve to be filled with gifts.

clue.text: Going to the front, place of duty for nurse

definitions.meaning: a nurse working in a hospital room is on the ward

explanation.surface: A nurse heading for the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means forward; split, it describes where a nurse is stationed in a hospital.

definitions.meaning: a sortie, a party of soldiers rushing out from a besieged place

explanation.surface: A young woman's witty remark at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, a military sortie by a group of troops, and a witty remark.

definitions.meaning: small stems with leaves cut from a plant

explanation.surface: Someone fixes up bits of mistletoe for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sprays of a plant; also small nails, so as a verb, fastens with such nails.

indicators.note: the letters are put through a change, a rearrangement into a new order

explanation.surface: Wishing for a fresh start in the coming year.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared at the end of 2006.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle was published just before 2007, so the coming twelve months were the year ahead.

clue.text: It's cold at the Pole, but not unpleasant

indicators.note: the word for cold is placed beside the pole letter

parts.note: N stands for the North Pole
ice is very cold, frozen water

explanation.surface: It may be freezing at the North Pole, but it is pleasant enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' could be a Polish person; here it is a magnetic pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant or agreeable, which is what not unpleasant amounts to.

parts.note: rent, as a past participle, means torn
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Hiring a party as a practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent-a-' suggests hire; it means torn. 'Wind-up' suggests a hoax, but is a winding wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating column of air is literally a wind that winds itself up.

clue.text: Form of decoration that has grown over the years

definitions.text: Form of decoration that has grown over the years

parts.words: Form of decoration that has grown over the years
parts.note: suggests a fashion that has spread, but means the Christmas decoration that literally grows

explanation.surface: A style of ornament that has become more popular over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas fir is decorated, and it has grown over many years before being cut.

definitions.meaning: waits are Christmas ... singers who go door to door

explanation.surface: A young woman waiting for the show to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Waits are bands of Christmas singers going from house to house.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and the festive song that street singers perform.

clue.text: A Christmas tree, for example, is always popular

definitions.meaning: a fir that keeps its leaves all year
enduringly liked, never going out of fashion

explanation.surface: Christmas trees never go out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant keeping its foliage all year, and something whose appeal never fades.
